caseno: First Appeal No. 282 of 2003 with Civil Rule No. 551 (fm) of 2002 Emarat Chairman
lawyer:
TH Khan with Mahbubey Alam and Rezina Chowdhury, Advocates ----- For the Appellant. 
MA Samad with MGH Ruhullah, Advocates ----- For the Respondent.
parties:
RAJUK ------ Appellant 
vs 
MN Alam and Associates Limited ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J : The Chairman, Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (in short, RAJUK) presented the appeal against the ex parte decree dated 15-5-02 passed by Joint District Judge, Court No.5 at Dhaka in Title Suit No.1 of 1999, which made the award dated 19-9-98 Rule of the Court. 

 4. On 3-2-99 the RAJUK appeared and after taking time, ultimately on 8-3-2000 filed an objection to the award. By order dated 7-5-2000 the objection was rejected by the learned Subordinate Judge as time barred, not in order as not supported by statutory security and non-acceptable on behalf of third party. Against said order the RAJUK moved this Division in Civil Revision No. 4778 of 2000, which was discharged by a Division Bench by order dated 18-11-01, 54 DLR 161. Then, by order dated 15-5-2000 the suit was decreed ex parte and the award was made Rule of the Court. 

 18. On behalf of the consultant, it is contended that the appellate Court in an appeal under section 17 of the Act cannot go behind the award of the arbitrator or judgment of the Court "except on the ground that it is in excess of, or not otherwise in accordance with, the decree." 

 "Judgment in terms of award-Where the Court sees no cause to remit the award or any of the matters referred to arbitration for reconsideration or to set aside the award, the Court shall, after the time for making an application to set aside has expired, or such application having been made, after refusing it, proceed to pronounce judgment according to the award, and upon the judgment so pronounced decree shall follow, and no appeal shall lie from such decree except on the ground that it is in excess of, or not otherwise in accordance with, the award." 

 20. Then, when the Court is satisfied on both of the requirements and after the time for objection to an award passed and/or the objection, if any filed, is rejected, it shall proceed to pronounce judgment in accordance with the award and upon the judgment so pronounced a decree shall follow. After going through such procedure, when the Court signs a decree, which could only be challenged on the ground that the decree is in excess of the award or not otherwise in accordance with the award. Scope of such an appeal is intended to be very limited. 

 22. Section 2(9) of the Code of Civil Procedure defines 'judgment' meaning the statement by the Judge of the grounds of decree or order. Order XX of the Code provides: 

 31. Recently, section 17 of the Act received close examination of the Supreme Court of India in the Union of India vs Manager, M/s Joy and Associates (2001) 3 SCC 277 = AIR 2001 (SC) 809. The union government made an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside an ex parte decree making an award Rule of the Court. The application was all through dismissed. It is the Supreme Court which allowed the application and set' aside the judgment and decree. Indian Supreme Court after thorough examination of section 17 with reference to the Code of Civil Procedure was also of the view that the Court is not exempted even when no one objects to the award from deciding whether the award should be sent back to the arbitration for modification and reconsideration of any matter or liable to be set aside before it goes to pronounce judgment according to the award. 

 32. We are therefore, of the view that when a Court after examination of the award for the purposes of making it Rule of the Court is satisfied that there is a valid arbitration agreement, reference made is valid, appointment of arbitrator or arbitrators is valid as per law and arbitration agreement, the award is in existence, only then it shall proceed to announce judgment. Grounds for satisfaction of the Court about the award could not be exhaustively enumerated nor could the Court be asked to write out specific grounds for his satisfaction. But the order that is judgment of the Court making the award Rule of Court, must show such satisfaction. A decree then shall follow the judgment. Such decree could only be challenged on the limited ground that the decree was in excess of the award or not in accordance with the award. 

 34. Order clearly shows that he was not at all aware of the duty cast upon him by section 17 of the Act. We have already found the award a nullity. We are therefore, unable to accept such judgment making the award Rule of the Court and the decree followed thereto. Appeal, therefore, succeeds. 

 35. In the result, the appeal is allowed with cost. Impugned judgment making the award Rule of the Court and decree followed thereto are hereby quashed and set aside.
